s1.syndrome_frame: Acute gastrointestinal bleeding with epigastric pain and a submucosal gastric lesion
salient_findings: Epigastric pain
Hematemesis
Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration
Low hemoglobin level (6.3 g/dL) that improved with transfusion
Well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation on CT
key_facts: One-week history of epigastric pain and hematemesis
No significant medical or surgical history
Hemoglobin level rose to 10 g/dL after transfusion
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass

shortlist.label: Gastric lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal lesion with fat attenuation on CT

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST)
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal lesion with no malignant features on biopsy

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Heterogeneous mass with fat attenuation on CT

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal lesion with potential for malignant transformation

raw.rationale: The presence of a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa and a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation on CT suggests a gastric lipoma, which is consistent with the biopsy showing no malignant features.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST)
rejected.why: GISTs are typically more aggressive and may have malignant features, which is not consistent with the biopsy results.

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are usually solid and homogeneous, whereas the CT scan showed a heterogeneous mass with fat attenuation.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are malignant tumors, which is not consistent with the biopsy showing no malignant features.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Leiomyosarcomas are also malignant tumors, which is not consistent with the biopsy showing no malignant features.
